title: Event Provenance Gateway and Shape-Assertion Pipeline
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: Our Console usage telemetry pipeline currently accepts a wide variety of event shapes from SDKs and backend services. This has led to frequent downstream failures in aggregation jobs and alert noise from malformed events. Existing validators reject some malformed payloads, but provenance (which service emitted the event, SDK version, host) is inconsistently captured, and rejection rates spike under bursty traffic.

Goal: Implement an Event Provenance Gateway and a Shape-Assertion Pipeline that: 1) centralizes source metadata capture (service, instance id, SDK version, environment), 2) validates event payloads against a canonical schema registry with progressive fallback rules, 3) enforces idempotency and deduplication at ingestion, 4) provides deterministic rejection reasons and SLI/SLO metrics, and 5) supports a staged rollout with retroactive rehydration for previously accepted-but-ambiguous events.

Acceptance criteria:
- Ingest path inserts/annotates provenance attributes for 100% of events (service, instance, hostname, sdk_version) documented in spec.
- Shape-assertion pipeline rejects malformed events with deterministic rejection codes (REJ_SCHEMA, REJ_MISSING_PROVENANCE, REJ_INVALID_ID) and logs single-line human-readable reason.
- Schema rejection rate < 0.5% at steady-state for top-10 customers (measured after 2 weeks) and pipeline backpressure gracefully rejects with 429 when buffer thresholds reached.
- All rejections and provenance annotations are visible in Console observability dashboard (ingest_rejections, ingest_latency_p50/p95, provenance_coverage).
- Migration runbook exists to enable gateway in canary then global rollout with automated rehydration for 30 days of raw events.

High-level design:
1) Edge Provenance Collector (stateless API gateway service): sits in front of existing event intake. Responsibilities: canonicalize incoming headers, synthesize provenance if missing (with heuristics), attach deterministic event_id when absent (sha256 of canonicalized payload prefix + timestamp truncated), sign provenance blob with gateway key for downstream verification.
2) Shape-Assertion Pipeline (streaming service): consumes from intake topic, performs schema lookup against the schema registry (primary: strict schema; secondary: compatibility-mode schema), runs shape assertions (required fields, types, enum checks), annotates the event with validation outcome and rejection code, writes accepted events to the normalized topic and rejected events to quarantine with a compact reason.
3) Idempotency & Dedup layer: Bloom filter + short-term LRU cache to dedupe duplicates within a 10 minute window; deterministic event_id used as dedupe key.
4) Backpressure & Throttling: circuit-breaker when validation lag exceeds threshold (configurable), returns HTTP 429 with body pointing to documented client retry/backoff guidance.
5) Observability: emit metrics: ingest_events_total, ingest_rejections_total{code}, ingest_latency_ms{p50,p95,p99}, provenance_coverage_ratio, dedupe_rate. Create Console dashboards and alerts (thresholds: rejection rate > 1% sustained for 15m, validation lag > 30s p95).

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict vs progressive validation: strict schemas prevent bad data but increase client breakage. We implement progressive fallback: if event fails strict schema and client is low-volume/new, route to quarantine and notify client; for high-volume (trusted) clients we can operate in compatibility-mode after engineer approval.
- Dedup accuracy vs memory: Bloom filter + LRU gives good memory profile but admits false positives (dropping some unique events). We accept small false-positive dedupe rate (<0.01%) rather than large memory footprint for full dedupe guarantees.
- Provenance synthesis: trying to infer missing provenance may introduce incorrect attribution. Synthesis only used for routing/observability; canonical provenance used for billing/SLAs must be provided by the producer or require stronger attestation.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (canary): Deploy Edge Provenance Collector behind a feature flag and route 1% of traffic; verify provenance_coverage and no increase in ingest latency above 5ms p95.
- Week 2 (validation): Enable Shape-Assertion Pipeline in passive mode (annotate but do not reject) for 10% traffic; generate enrichment metrics and top rejection reasons; send Qs to product/SDK owners.
- Week 3 (controlled reject): Enable rejection for new clients and low-volume clients only; create self-serve console page for SDK owners to claim their failures.
- Week 4 (global): Full enforcement with quarantine + 30-day retention for rehydration.

Testing and QA:
- Unit and integration tests for schema assertions using full schema corpus in repo.
- End-to-end load test with realistic event mixes: bursty workloads, malformed event injection, duplicate flood. Use k6 + data-sim.
- Chaos test: simulate schema registry latency and downstream sink outage.

Monitoring and runbook:
- Dashboards: "Ingest Health", "Provenance Coverage", "Rejection Reasons".
- Alerts: pager for P0 incidents (validation lag > 2m p99 or global rejection rate spike > 5%).
- Runbook: steps to toggle passive/active validation, clear quarantine, rehydrate events via Dataflow job, rollback gateway. Add playbook links.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.example.com/display/ENG/Event+Provenance+Gateway 
- Schema registry proto: https://git.redwood.example.com/schemas/console-usage/proto/README.md
- Ingest PR: https://git.redwood.example.com/ingest/protocols/pull/487
- Load test results (k6): https://perf.redwood.example.com/runs/ingest-2026-02-28
- Quarantine viewer prototype: https://console.redwood.example.com/quarantine-preview

Open questions:
- Should the gateway sign provenance with per-customer keys (KMS) or a single service key? (security raised per-customer as preferred for audits).
- How long should we keep deterministic event_id for dedupe across restarts? (proposal: 10 minutes default, configurable per-customer).

Next steps:
- Finish PR for Edge Provenance Collector (linked above) and get engineering review from @Maya Wong and @Liam O'Connor.
- Build passive-mode Shape-Assertion Pipeline and deploy to canary environment.
- Partner with SDK team to surface client-level error dashboards and onboarding guidance.
